topic.title: Long-Context Memory and KV-Cache Efficiency
topic.area: Language Models and Natural Language Processing
topic.overview: Long-context language models must retain useful past information without letting attention memory dominate inference cost. This cluster studies key-value cache compression, eviction, recomputation, sparse attention, and recurrent summaries. Methods differ in whether discarded information can be recovered and whether importance is estimated for the current query or learned across contexts.
topic.whyItMatters: A bounded cache can speed decoding yet silently erase information needed much later. Efficiency therefore has to be assessed alongside long-range retrieval, multi-turn consistency, and sensitivity to aggressive compression.
topic.evolution: Early representatives investigate cache-based language models, memory access, and parallel decoding. The 2024–2025 work targets bandwidth and token selection. Recent methods learn eviction policies, preserve evicted content in latent memory, and exploit shared low-rank structure across layers, extending the design space beyond simply keeping fewer tokens.
openQuestions: How can a model recognize that an evicted detail has become important?
Which memory tests predict failure in realistic multi-turn workloads?
